look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: Is this a rhizomatous upright herb, rather than a large woody sagebrush shrub? Check the soft silvery or two-toned stem leaves (entire, toothed or lobed), then the many small, inconspicuous flower heads in a narrow to branched cluster. Leaf color alone cannot confirm the species.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Aromatic, spreading rhizomatous perennial herb, typically 20–80 cm tall; stems erect, simple or branched, often hairy.

key_traits.label: Leaves attachment
key_traits.text: Leaves along stems, linear to broadly elliptic, about 1.5–11 cm long; margins entire, toothed or variably lobed; gray-green, white-silvery or two-toned with hairs. Variation includes subspecies.

key_traits.label: Flower reproductive
key_traits.text: Small disciform heads grouped in compact or open branched arrays, erect to nodding; involucres approximately 2–4 mm with densely woolly gray-green phyllaries; ray florets absent.

key_traits.label: Fruit seed
key_traits.text: Tiny dry one-seeded cypselae, around 0.5 mm; no conspicuous pappus.

key_traits.label: Stem bud
key_traits.text: Look for herbaceous upright stems and spreading rhizomes; do not identify solely from gray foliage.
